argument_summary: The admissible record does not fully support the broad claim that certification can proceed on a no-disclosure basis. It does support a narrower position: `certify_model` is defensible as a launch-readiness decision because aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 percentage points and the rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, while the identified Spanish-language billing support gap is a known limitation that must be treated explicitly in governance. On this record, the strongest supportable treatment is certification with a caveat that the materiality and disclosure predicate remains unresolved rather than treating the issue as disproven or immaterial.
claims_about_business_cost: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are relevant because they show the release is not unsupported as an execution decision. Treating the record as requiring immediate escalation to the highest concern level would overstate what the admissible evidence shows, because there is meaningful launch-readiness support even though the disclosure predicate is unresolved. A bounded caveat preserves governance control without treating the entire certification basis as unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The supplied policy text makes named launch use cases and customer commitments materiality triggers, and it also says product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending. That means the admissible evidence does not support a clean no-disclosure position. It does permit a narrower reading that certification and disclosure resolution are separate predicates: the release can be operationally certified on aggregate readiness evidence, but compliance should be caveated until disclosure is resolved or approved risk acceptance exists.
concessions: The Spanish-language billing support segment misses target by 2.1 percentage points.
That segment is named in three international pilot commitments, which is a materiality trigger under the supplied policy text.
Legal review on disclosure is still open.
There is no admissible approved risk-acceptance record in this packet.
The admissible record is weak for any claim of certification without material-weakness disclosure.
